transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-12-09
Start: 14:00 PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Ruiz (CISO, Argus), Evan Holt (Platform Eng), Sanjay Patel (Director Data Privacy), Rina Kapoor (Infra)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Security posture discovery focused on compliance and deployment modes. ACTIONS: share SOC2/ISO, schedule infra deep dive, provide sample SLA/pricing for Dedicated.

00:00 Jordan Blake: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm jordan from redwood inference, im the AE on this. quick intros?
00:12 Maya Ruiz: hi maya ruiz, ciso at argus, thanks for setting this up. we're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for PII and PHI workloads.
00:20 Evan Holt: evan here, platform eng, i'll be working through network, vpc details, and deployment constraints.
00:28 Jordan: great, high level we'll run through our attestation posture (soc2, iso), SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, and retention. then dig into what private/dedicated looks like.
00:40 Priya Desai: quick note, i might jump in with more technical answers.

02:05 Sanjay Patel: first question — do you have SOC 2 Type II? and are you ISO27001 certified? and do you provide penetration test reports?
02:14 Jordan: yes we are SOC 2 Type II; we also have ISO27001. i'll share the artifacts after the call. we also have an internal pen test summary and third-party pentest reports we can provide redacted.
02:32 Maya: what's the turnaround on that? we need evidence for our procurement and compliance teams within a week ideally.
02:38 Jordan: we can send the certified reports and the pen test summary by tomorrow morning, i'll drop those in the CRM.

05:10 Evan: on auth — we operate Okta for SSO; we need SAML2.0 and SCIM for user provisioning. does redwood support SAML + SCIM and can we map roles to SAML groups?
05:23 Priya: yes, Redwood supports SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC can be configured and you can map SAML groups to role levels in the console. there is also an API if you want programmatic user sync.
05:45 Evan: any limitations on role granularity? we have roles for dev/prod/data-ops and want fine grained audit separation.
05:54 Priya: you can create custom roles and policies for routes/models. audit logs capture token-level actions and admin changes, with timestamps and actor identity. retaining logs is configurable (we keep 90 days by default for hosted, can extend).

08:30 Rina Kapoor: on audit logs and tamper-evidence — do you provide write-once logs or an external log export to our SIEM?
08:42 Liam Chen: we support streaming audit logs to your SIEM (splunk/elk/azure monitor) via secure push. logs include request metadata, model used, token counts, and admin changes. we also support immutable archival to your s3 bucket for long term retention.
08:58 Rina: ok good. does that include payloads? we can't have PII in logs — we need redaction or option to disable payload logging.
09:10 Priya: by default hosted doesn't persist full request payloads in long-term logs, and you can configure to redact or not store input/output in audit exports. for Dedicated and Private you can fully control retention and payload storage.

11:45 Maya: encryption — do you offer customer-managed keys (CMEK) and HSM integration? we require CMEK in the EU region.
11:56 Jordan: yes, Dedicated and Private support CMEK via KMS (cloud provider KMS or your existing KMS). for Private on-prem deployments we can integrate with your HSM or KMS appliance; for hosted we use provider-managed KMS but we do offer an HSM-backed option for enterprise.
12:20 Sanjay: what's the key rotation policy and can we audit key usage?
12:28 Priya: key rotation follows standard KMS rotation for provider KMS; for CMEK you control rotation. we expose key usage logs and can integrate key access logs into your audit pipeline.

14:00 Evan: data residency — our data must remain in EU for certain flows. are there region guarantees and controls for routing?
14:10 Liam: yes, we support region pinning. Hosted can be region-specific (EU) with data in region. Dedicated gives you fixed capacity in chosen region, and Private means you own the infra. we also have smart routing to failover to compatible regions if you request it, but for compliance you can lock down routing to avoid cross-region failover.

16:40 Maya: for Private deployment — do you have a private control plane or is it a fully air-gapped option?
16:49 Priya: we offer two patterns: a private control plane (Redwood control plane lives in our managed plane but can run in your VPC with mutual TLS) or a fully on-prem package that is air-gapped. most regulated customers pick the private control plane in their VPC for manageability.
17:10 Sanjay: that private control plane — would Redwood still have admin access? we need strict separation and auditability.
17:19 Jordan: admin access can be limited; for Dedicated we offer role separation and for Private you control keys and have full audit. we can set up defined service accounts and just-in-time support access with recorded sessions and require customer approval for sensitive ops.

19:30 Evan: performance questions — if we go Dedicated and pin GPUs, how does key management work for KV cache and inference keys — is anything stored in plaintext on the instance?
19:45 Priya: no plaintext. KV cache is in-memory and ephemeral; we encrypt at rest for checkpointing. inference request tokens are processed in memory; when you request persistence for caching we encrypt with your CMEK.

22:02 Maya: about retention — how configurable is deletion? we need ability to purge all customer data within X days and to provide certificate of destruction.
22:14 Liam: we support configurable retention policies per customer and per route. for Hosted we provide configurable windows and deletion requests; for Dedicated/Private you can set aggressive retention and we provide logs of deletion operations. we can also run a certified purge and provide attestation for the pilot.

24:30 Sanjay: legal/procurement angle — what does indemnity look like and do you sign data processing agreements and security addendums?
24:45 Jordan: yes DPA + security addendum are standard. we have template terms for Dedicated and Private. indemnity limits are negotiable at enterprise stage; i'll surface our legal contact and a template.

27:05 Evan: for SSO we also need SCIM provisioning and automated deprovisioning when employees leave. latency on deprovision propagation is important.
27:18 Priya: SCIM delta sync within minutes; immediate deprovision via API. we can also optionally disable tokens issued by a user when account deactivated.

29:40 Maya: can you share an example network diagram for VPC peering and egress rules? specifically for private control plane models how does traffic flow?
29:52 Liam: yes, we'll share a standard diagram — control plane in your VPC with private endpoints, nodes in a customer-managed subnet, and a bastion/ops plane for upgrades. traffic flow: control plane calls outbound to update checks but data paths stay intra-VPC unless you opt into telemetry exports.

32:00 Sanjay: threat modelling — do you have documented controls for insider risk, privileged access, and separation of duties?
32:10 Jordan: yes, our SOC2 controls detail access control, privileged access reviews, and separation of duties. for Private deployments we adopt your internal policies where applicable.

34:20 Maya: benchmark / pilot — we want to run a 2-week pilot for PHI workflows. what do you need from us to scope that?
34:32 Priya: for pilot we'll need expected qps, average sequence length, and payload size. also sample prompts (sanitized) helps for quality tuning. we'll provide a test plan and propose a small dedicated pool or private deployment depending on volume.
34:50 Evan: expected qps is around 20 req/s for our peak flows, average token lengths ~800, burst up to 40.
35:02 Priya: noted. that profile suggests Dedicated with autoscale/burst is a good fit to keep latency predictable. we can propose batching and caching settings to control cost.

37:10 Jordan: recap — we'll send SOC2/ISO and pen test summary; share sample VPC diagram and Dedicated pricing; schedule infra deep dive for next week (proposed 2026-12-16).
37:26 Maya: sounds good. also need the legal templates and DPA.
37:32 Jordan: yes, i'll include them.

39:00 Rina: small question — are there maintenance windows and how are updates handled in Private?
39:10 Liam: for Private on-prem, updates are via customer-approved upgrade packages; for private control plane in your VPC we coordinate maintenance windows and offer canary rollouts and automatic fallback.

41:20 Sanjay: any red flags? for us, biggest one is audit log integrity and key custody.
41:29 Priya: audit log streaming to your SIEM + CMEK means you can control custody and retention; we'll provide attestation of immutable archival if needed.

43:00 Jordan: ok thank you all; next steps as discussed. i'll follow up with the docs tomorrow.
43:10 Maya: thanks everyone.

End of recording.
